tasks.short: Contact insurers to resolve billing issues

steps.what: Review billing issues and verify the relevant claim and insurer response
Assemble claim evidence and billing reference details for insurer contact
Contact insurance companies and resolve or escalate the billing issue
Record billing resolution and any further action needed

tasks.design: Configure a contact-pack view in the pharmacy billing system {OTHER}, with claim references and selected supporting documents from {DOCS}. The pharmacist checks the pack, contacts the insurer through the existing phone or {PARTNER_PORTAL} route and records the outcome; no claim correction or dispute concession is automatic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is repeatedly located and assembled before discussing a rejected or disputed claim.
tasks.enabler_now: Native claim views and document templates can reduce assembly without interpreting coverage automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Clarifying an insurer's reasoning and agreeing a resolution when facts or rules conflict.
tasks.human_edge: The pharmacist can recognise an unsafe disclosure or an unjustified correction and escalate it.
tasks.altitude: Less evidence assembly; insurer negotiation and financial decisions retain their time and authority.

reach.task: Locate the authorised source document needed to clarify a disputed claim
reach.learn: Minimum necessary disclosure and claim traceability

evidence.claim: Native evidence-pack views can reduce claim-document assembly while insurer discussion remains manual; the time allocation is model knowledge, not a documented pharmacy billing case.

assumptions: Boundary is pharmacist handling of an insurer billing issue, excluding insurer labour, original claim submission and later financial adjustment. Actual European payer arrangements must be confirmed rather than importing an overseas insurance model.

Pharmacist produces claim identifier, patient account, service date, billed amount, insurer, response text, issue description and source references in s1 with all 30 hours retained. No structured discrepancy code is assumed; free-text responses are read manually.
s2 retains 12 hours for field capture, source selection, disclosure checks and pack verification. Missing identifiers or source documents require manual retrieval; the view never infers eligibility.

Test native views before custom code. Existing claim screens earn no new saving. s3 retains all contact and disclosure decisions; s4 retains outcome capture and follow-up decisions. No new automatic external action is introduced.
unknowns: Local insurer contact routes and claim-record access
Current pack assembly burden and disclosure policy
research_questions: Does a checked contact pack reduce preparation and repeat contacts without increasing wrong-account or excess-data disclosure?

already_counted.description: Billing interpretation and structured source capture
Evidence selection, pack checking and missing-document exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain pack fields, access controls and source links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=30+12+40+10=92; gross 8 minus 2 upkeep gives net 6. High assumes repeated evidence assembly; low removes only 2 hours, consumed by upkeep. Interpretation, insurer discussion and outcome recording keep all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce preparation for insurer billing contact while retaining dispute resolution and financial accountability.
reach: Work with records specialists on traceable, limited claim evidence
role.ambitious_version: A pharmacist who enters insurer discussions with checked evidence and retains clear ownership of clinical and billing uncertainty.
